title: Review: today's smime-tree/mime-tree work
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — Two dead public enum variants (AllTrustAnchorsExpired, PathLenViolated), a known pkix-chain algorithm support gap affecting P-384 CA chains in production, a doc/code mismatch in agree_ecdh that will mislead implementors, and a padding oracle in DecryptionFailed error strings.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: MIME-r5p.3 (anchor/pkix divergence — depends on pkix-chain internals not inspected), MIME-r5p.6 (UKM SharedInfo — depends on RFC 5753 KDF spec reading). Uncertainty driven by: pkix-chain source not read directly, only interface and error types consulted; EccCmsSharedInfo entity_u_info behavior with non-None UKM not traced through the KDF call. Would raise confidence if: read pkix-chain verify_chain_default source; run a UKM-bearing OpenSSL KARI fixture against this code.
mime-tree/tests confidence: 75% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: MIME-r5p.17 (walk.rs in_alternative nullification scope — RFC 8621 §4.1.4 JS pseudocode is ambiguous on whether all isInline types or only text/* trigger nullification; the reference algorithm text is the only authoritative source and requires reading the exact JS), MIME-r5p.7 (qp_input_was_limited false negative — this is a narrow edge case when 4*max_bytes exactly equals body_bytes.len() and the QP content is dense enough that decoded < max_bytes). Uncertainty driven by: (1) RFC 8621 §4.1.4 JS pseudocode not directly read in this session — relied on comments and test cases as proxy, (2) smime_tests.rs KARI fixtures are complex enough that a mis-structured fixture might pass structural checks while being wrong cryptographically, (3) walk.rs cross-population logic (lines 168-188) has corner cases in multipart/alternative with both text and html that are not fully exercised by the 7 unit tests.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Code is Rust idiomatic overall. Main gaps: SmimeError missing Serialize+Deserialize (violates stated invariant), sig_verify generic closures could be impl Fn, and the PartialEq coupling to der::Error. No .unwrap() outside tests, no Box<dyn Error> in API, all public error types have Display. #[non_exhaustive] applied correctly throughout.
mime-tree idiom rating: CLEAN — no unwrap() outside tests, no .len()==0, no index loops, no format!("{}",x), no gratuitous clones. TransferEncoding and ParseError are #[non_exhaustive]. All public structs derive required traits. Early returns are guard clauses, idiomatic. Option<&mut Vec> in walk.rs is unusual but necessary to model RFC 8621 shared-nullable semantics without heap allocation.
Rust idiom confidence: 80% chance no missed issue. Uncertainty: der::Error PartialEq not verified; clippy not run.
Pass 2 idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No new P1/P2 findings. One new P3 (MIME-r5p.55: ukm Vec allocation in try_decrypt_kari). The four existing P2 issues (MIME-r5p.28, .29, .53, .54) are all real: .28 per-byte CRLF push still present in decode.rs, .29 issuer DER re-encode inside find() closure still present in cert.rs, .53 description corrected (one monomorphization not three, impl Fn is still marginally more idiomatic), .54 trust_anchors slice typing is an opinion-level point. Changed files are otherwise clean: deprecated variants are correctly annotated with #[allow(deprecated)] on Display impl, is_encoding_problem field is properly documented and populated, collect::<Result<_,_>>() is used correctly.
Pass 2 confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) KARI multi-RecipientInfo behavioral change (filed as MIME-r5p.56 at P2) — the exact CMS message structure that would trigger the early-exit is unusual enough that no test exists for it; (2) the OpenSSL oracle step in Test E uses SystemTime::now() for signing but a fixed historical time for smime-tree verify() — the two time windows diverge if the test cert is near expiry, but certs expire 2036-04-29 so this is not currently a problem; (3) the #[deprecated] variants on CertChainError — Serde round-trip of serialized data containing these variants still works, but no test exercises deserialization of legacy payloads. All fixes reviewed: KARI restructuring is correct (recipient-first check is the right ordering); anchor_subjects DER error propagation is correct (fail-fast is strictly better); is_encoding_problem field addition is correctly initialized in all construction paths (parse.rs, decode.rs tests); #[deprecated] variants are correctly handled with #[allow(deprecated)] on the Display impl; OpenSSL oracle step in Test E is structurally identical to existing Test C which already passes.
